messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] error in gcRMA background correction
parts:
Hi 'shouhermione',

in order to do gcRMA background correction the chip type (and the CDF)
has to have MMs, and more specifically (PM,MM) pairs. See

Wu, Z.; Irizarry, R.; Gentleman, R.; Murillo, F. M. & Spencer, F. A
Model Based Background Adjustment for Oligonucleotide Expression
Arrays #JASA#, Berkeley Electronic Press, 2004, 99, 909-917

and the 'gcrma' package for details.

I don't know if there are such pairs on the HuEx-1_0-st-v2 chip type
(design), but at least the HuEx-1_0-st-v2,coreR2,A20071112,EP.CDF does
not contain it;

cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$byChipType("HuEx-1_0-st-v2",
tags="coreR2,A20071112,EP");
isPm <- isPm(cdf);
isMm <- !isPm;
print(summary(isMm));
## Mode FALSE
## logical 1082385

The next release will do a initial test for this and give an
informative error message.

Cheers

Henrik

I mean the PM-GCBG correction which estimates the background of a
specific PM probe by the median intensities of those BGP probes on an
exon array that have the same GC content as the perfect match probe
referred above.

Does it make sense? As an undergraduate student, I am not very
familiar with this field and is making my effort learning fundamental
things.

Thank you!


Shou

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: error in gcRMA background correction
parts:
Hi Shou,

no worries, we are all learning something new every day and so did I
from your question. I never heard of this method before, but then
I've also haven't done much work on exon arrays. I'm sure Elizabeth
P, Mark R, Ken S and other exon gurus know about this though.
However, I'm quite sure there is currently no implementation available
in aroma.affymetrix that does "PM-GCBG correction".

I searched for it online and found the following white paper by Affymetrix:

Exon Array Background Correction, Revision Date: 2005-09-27, Revision
Version: 1.0
http://www.affymetrix.com/support/technical/whitepapers/exon_background_correction_whitepaper.pdf

It doesn't look impossible to implement, but it would require
annotation data with GC counts/content for each probe etc, which is a
bit tricky to get/use today. I'm slowly adding transparent support
for probe-sequence information and when that is in place the GC-count
information will be a piece of cake, but before that it is probably
not worth spending time trying to implement it.

Cheers

/Henrik

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: error in gcRMA background correction
parts:
Hi all.

Indeed, I am aware of PM-GCBG method, but I have not used it. I
believe there is also a version of GCRMA BG correction that takes
(instead of MM probes) a bunch of negative control probes. I haven't
used this either.

It would be desirable to have both of these implemented within
aroma.affymetrix, but it is not currently high my on priority list.

You can use RMA BG correction.

Mark

messages.author: fd467cdb4718031f
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: error in gcRMA background correction
parts:
Dear Shou et al,
The DABG correction has been implemented in the Affymetrix Power Tools
(APT), a set of command line tools.
the tool in question is: apt-probeset-summarize
If you use Windows, then I believe that the free Affy Expression
Console may let you run DABG, since this uses the APT toolkit.
You will also need the library file for your chip, which includes the
clf/pgf plus the 'bgp' file which is the crucial part for fitting DABG.

It's easy to import this output into R, but I don't know how to get
this into an aroma.affymetrix friendly format.
Mark R: perhaps we can talk about implementing this if these requests
become more frequent.

URLs:
APT: http://www.affymetrix.com/support/developer/powertools/changelog/index.html
Affy library files: http://www.affymetrix.com/support/technical/libraryfilesmain.affx
apt-probeset-summarise: http://www.affymetrix.com/support/developer/powertools/changelog/apt-probeset-summarize.html

cheers,
Mark
-----------------------------------------------------
Mark Cowley, BSc (Bioinformatics)(Hons)

Peter Wills Bioinformatics Centre
Garvan Institute of Medical Research, Sydney, Australia
-----------------------------------------------------
